canonicalStep.title: oil-drain-plug-identify (BMW 328i draft Engine Oil & Filter Change guide; evidence step 5)

elements.describe: The engine oil drain plug seen end-on: a short plain external hex head (17 mm size) with a flat copper-coloured crush washer under the head.
A thin flat copper-coloured crush washer sitting between the plug head and the oil pan surface.
The oil pan surface around the plug, drawn as a plain simplified matte aluminium-grey surface.
Oil pan perimeter screws, casting ribs and nearby bolts.

Not established for this car: sources conflict (straight down vs facing right vs sideways) and the automatic pan is not catalogued. Oil pan variant: Turner lists separate engine oil pans for manual (11137553164) and automatic (11137552414) cars; the RealOEM 328i diagram shows only the manual pan (S205A = No). This car is an automatic (S205), so plug position and orientation on ITS pan are not established; keep the pan a plain generic mass.

establishes: N52: drain plug is behind a small removable access panel on the underside; panel shape and fasteners differ by poster (a triangular panel; three screws); plug orientation reports differ (straight down vs facing right).

establishes: E90/E91/E92/E93 DIY: the drain bolt is behind an access hatch just behind the front-centre jack point, opened with a coin; 17 mm socket on a ratchet; copper crush washer replaced each time; the pan is placed a few inches to the right of the bolt.
references.rights: Text consulted for facts only; no pixels or images from this source are used.

establishes: 17 mm plug with copper crush washer; oil exits sideways.
